arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: David Goldberg argued Clark lost his fair trial right. He stated Arizona law required proof of intent.
General Clement argued Arizona's law is constitutional. He stated the state controls the defense definition.
Justice Kennedy asked if the state deemed testimony irrelevant. He sought clarification on the state's position.

paragraphs: This case tests state power to define insanity. It also tests limits on mental state evidence.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: Clark wants the Court to strike down Arizona's insanity law. He seeks to admit his mental state evidence.
Arizona wants the Court to uphold its insanity law. It seeks to keep mental state evidence excluded.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: Clark argues Arizona violated his Fourteenth Amendment rights. He claims the state barred relevant evidence.
Arizona argues it has discretion to define the insanity defense. It claims the Constitution allows this choice.

sections.heading: What the justices asked
paragraphs: Justice Ginsburg asked about the name guilty except insane. She questioned what specific crime Clark committed.
Justice Breyer asked if Clark knew right from wrong. He questioned the cognitive element of the defense.
